cards.d: If you are astounded, you are very surprised.
cards.e: I was astounded that Monica won the art competition.

cards.d: An attribute is a characteristic of a person or thing.
cards.e: He isn’t very clever, but he does have some other positive attributes.

cards.d: If someone is bilingual, then they can speak two languages.
cards.e: Since you already know English, after learning French you’ll be bilingual.

cards.d: A clone is an identical copy of a living creature.
cards.e: Scientists recently made a clone of a sheep.

cards.d: Colloquial describes informal words that are more suitable for speech than writing.
cards.e: I find it difficult to understand people if they use colloquial language.

cards.d: Cosmetics are substances that make the face and skin more beautiful.
cards.e: Girls often look nicer when they don’t use so many cosmetics.

cards.d: To dash means to run or move quickly.
cards.e: Helen dashed up the stairs, so she wouldn’t be late for her appointment.

cards.d: Disgust is a feeling of distaste and anger caused by something rude or unpleasant.
cards.e: He felt disgust toward his date because she had such terrible eating habits.

cards.d: If something is fluorescent, it is such a bright color that it seems to give off light.
cards.e: She highlighted the key words in the document with a fluorescent yellow pen.

cards.d: If you are furious, you are extremely angry.
cards.e: My father was furious when he read my bad school report.

cards.d: A gulf is a gap between people who do not understand each other.
cards.e: There has been a gulf between James and Tony since their parents died.

cards.d: Humanities are subjects which analyze human ideas, such as history and literature.
cards.e: Jennifer has always been more interested in humanities than science.

cards.d: A knot is made when you tie the ends of rope or cord together.
cards.e: He tied a knot in his shoelaces, so they wouldn’t come off during the race.

cards.d: A linguist is someone who studies languages.
cards.e: Tony is a good linguist and speaks four different languages.

cards.d: A participant is someone who joins in a social event or competition.
cards.e: There were thousands of participants in this year’s marathon.

cards.d: If something is plausible, it is reasonable or possible.
cards.e: It is plausible that Jack isn’t here today because he is sick.

cards.d: A ritual is a formal custom that people do regularly.
cards.e: Ken was very interested to learn about the religious rituals of the natives.

cards.d: A sibling is a brother or sister.
cards.e: Jane has two siblings, an older brother and a younger sister.

cards.d: If someone is skinny, they are extremely thin.
cards.e: Polly is very skinny. I think she needs to eat more.

cards.d: If something is vague, it is not clear, and it gives very few details.
cards.e: I asked him about his mother’s health, but he was very vague about it.
